REDTRACE
Project Documentation

Team Out of Galaxy NASA Space Challenge

1. Project Overview

REDTRACE is an integrated, interactive exploration map of Jezero Crater, Mars as this part of Mars we have its information. It combines NASA datasets into one interface so astronauts can understand terrain, identify obstacles, find scientifically interesting places, and plan safe routes for surface exploration.

A user first creates an account and signs in. They then see the map of Mars, choose which data layers to display, place rest stops at specific locations, and add newly discovered places with information and a photo as evidence.

Project name

REDTRACE

Team

Out of Galaxy

Location

Jezero Crater, Mars

Challenge

Interplanetary Survival Guide

Team Members

Ahmed Ehab - Mohamed Khaled Ashour – Yassin Tamer
Marwa Yahia - Hana Darwish - Salma Hesham

2. Problem Statement

NASA has collected enormous amounts of Mars data through many missions. However, these datasets are scattered across different platforms. Astronauts need combined information to understand terrain, identify obstacles, and plan safe exploration routes.

Existing tools such as JPL’s Mars Trek and the USGS-NASA Planetary Geologic Mapping Program are built for regional and global views, and they do not let an explorer save personal rest stops or record new findings.

The question we address: how can we turn scattered Mars data into one integrated exploration map?

3. Proposed Solution

REDTRACE is a web platform that brings the data together in one place. It allows users to:

  • Create an account and sign in.
  • Visualize different layers of Mars data and choose which ones to show.
  • Identify potential terrain obstacles to support safer route planning.
  • Explore points of interest supported by NASA images and data.
  • Make rest stops at specific places on the map.
  • Add a newly discovered place with information and a picture as evidence.

Data layers offered:

Layer

What it shows

Thermal

Surface temperature information

Topographic

Elevation, slopes, and terrain

Geological

Rock formations and surface composition

Optical

High-resolution surface images

4. System Architecture

REDTRACE follows a standard web application design with a React frontend, a .net

backend, and supporting storage and data sources.

System architecture of REDTRACE

Component

Role

User (browser)

Opens the web application on a computer or tablet

React frontend

Login and sign-up pages, interactive map, layer selection, forms for rest stops and discoveries

.Net backend

Handles authentication, serves map and layer data, and saves user content

Database

Stores user accounts, rest stops, and discovered places 

Image storage

Stores the evidence photos uploaded with discoveries 

NASA and USGS data

NASA Mars Trek, USGS-NASA Planetary Geologic Maps, Perseverance raw images, and the NASA Planetary Data System

Typical flow: the user signs in, the frontend requests the map and chosen layers from the backend, the backend returns the data, and when the user saves a rest stop or discovery, the backend writes it to the database and stores any photo.
